title: Randomized source cues and separate sharing and belief measures
rationale: The source study found misinformation lowered sharing by 18.2 points and plausibility by 18.6 points, so the two moved together. High trust (+5.7) and close tie (+3.0) were associated with more sharing, but sharer attributes were not randomized and both outcomes were forced choices. Randomizing source cues and rating sharing and accuracy separately lets the two outcomes diverge.
contribution: Tests causally whether source trust and tie strength shift sharing intent more than perceived accuracy of a false headline.
limitations: Fictional contact lacks real relationship history
Incentivized share is a subsample with a small stake
Single headline per respondent limits topic generalization
Stated trust and tie are vignette cues, not real relationships

design.title: Randomized source cues and separate sharing and belief measures
design.overview: US Latino adults see one headline (true, false or fact-check) attributed to a fictional contact whose tie (close or distant) and trust (high or low) are randomized, giving a 3x2x2 factorial. They rate sharing intent and perceived accuracy on separate 1-7 scales, then make a real share-or-not choice.
design.hypothesis: Source trust and tie strength raise sharing intent more than perceived accuracy, especially for the false headline.
design.primaryOutcome: Sharing intent (1-7) minus perceived accuracy (1-7, standardized), and each rating separately.
design.comparison: High vs low trust and close vs distant tie, on sharing versus accuracy, by headline type.
design.population: US Latino adults from YouGov, stratified by survey language (English or Spanish).

questions.text: This is a research survey about how people respond to news posts. It takes about 8 minutes and is voluntary. Do you agree to take part?
Imagine {{ed:tie}} who you {{ed:trust}} shared this post: {{ed:headline_true}}
Imagine {{ed:tie}} who you {{ed:trust}} shared this post: {{ed:headline_false}}
Imagine {{ed:tie}} who you {{ed:trust}} shared this post: {{ed:headline_fc}}
How likely would you be to share this post? (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely)
Based on the available information, how likely is this post to be accurate? (1 = very unlikely, 7 = very likely)
Would you like us to post this item to a public feed under the study's account, with a note that you chose to share it? You will receive a small bonus either way.
Thank you. The contact was fictional, and the false headline was false. The correct information is that the claim is unsupported by evidence. Your responses are confidential.

assumptions: Power target: about 1000 per arm to detect 0.05 at 80% power (observed trust effect 0.057, MDE 0.051); about 1,300 per cell is needed for the tie effect of 0.03 under clustering.

Tie and trust (close/distant, high/low) are randomized within each headline arm via the survey platform; the flow shows one default setting per arm, and the full 3x2x2 crossing is implemented in the platform.
The real-share choice is asked of a random subsample.
Stratify by survey language (English or Spanish).
